reason: B is the better, though incomplete, proposal because a buried CrN layer is more plausible as a high-temperature diffusion barrier compatible with Cr, whereas A extrapolates a 5 nm Al2O3 barrier demonstrated only to 600 °C to 1100–1200 °C, where reaction with Zr and loss of continuity are serious concerns. B still needs a specified thickness, exact exposure times, and directly relevant evidence for CrN stability in steam and under irradiation.
